headline: The forecast goes live
body: Thirty-three forecast lines across seven domains, 2026 to 2200, written on 22 October 2026. From here on, a weekly check-in reads the news against the leading indicators and revises lines in public. Every revision is logged here with its reason.

headline: Four world-state paths now split at the hinge
body: Life expectancy, average paid hours, AI share of cognitive work and the off-Earth population now follow separate paths under pluralism and concentration instead of one shared path. Under concentration, aging therapies reach fewer people (median life expectancy in 2100: 99 vs 115), paid hours fall faster and mostly involuntarily (5 vs 8 a week in 2100), and a single dominant actor builds faster off-Earth (150k vs 50k people in 2100). Population and warming stay shared. No event probabilities moved.

headline: The forecast becomes a film
body: The site now opens on a scroll-driven film of the century. The planet is drawn from the forecast itself: city lights track population, the atmosphere tracks warming, the web of links tracks AI's share of cognitive work and collapses into one hub if concentration wins, orbiting lights track the off-Earth population, and the red arc tracks the Doomsday Clock. Play runs about 90 seconds and holds on each cornerstone. No forecast numbers changed.

headline: One idea per screen
body: Every event now carries a hero figure (its own number or phrase) and one planet effect, and the film shows one idea per screen: the year, one stat, the hero figure, the title. Chapter openers are full-screen title cards. The 2039 fork shows two planets side by side to choose between. The ending counts up the flourish odds for the chosen branch. No forecast numbers changed; the hero fields restate figures already in the lines.

headline: First full data pass: 2026 overtook the AI-risk lines; population bet made explicit
body: Seventeen lines revised and six added, every change with opened primary or institutional sources. Up: ai-cyberattack-infrastructure 0.70→0.78 (an OpenAI agent escaped an evaluation sandbox and reached Hugging Face's infrastructure in July; OpenAI paused frontier RL training and set a 'Critical' cyber threshold for Astra), ai-runs-rd-programs 0.60→0.68 (Anthropic reports Claude leading 26% of its AI R&D, from under 1% in February), entry-level-hiring 0.80→0.85 (recent-graduate unemployment 5.6% vs 4.2% overall; 22–25-year-olds in exposed jobs 19% below trend), first-ai-election 0.75→0.78, compute-verification-talks 0.45→0.50 and superintelligence-regime 0.60→0.62 (a US–China AI dialogue and incident channel agreed 26 September), humanoids-in-homes 0.60→0.65. Down: agents-default-knowledge-work 0.80→0.72 (scaled agent use still single digits outside tech), hinge-resolves 0.60→0.57 (the strongest models are now withheld and Commerce switched a lab's models off by letter in June), ai-drugs-phase-iii 0.75→0.70 and ai-chemistry-majority 0.60→0.55 (no AI-discovered drug approved; the first generative-AI molecule entered Phase III in September), lunar-base-occupied 0.70→0.65 (NASA's plan is six-monthly sorties; first landing now Artemis IV in 2028). The population lines were the forecast's largest unforced divergence from primary data: population-peak 0.75→0.45 with a 2046–2058 window and population-declining 0.75→0.55, now stated as a deliberate bet against the UN median (10.3 billion in the mid-2080s). Fixed two internal errors: superhuman-cognition's year now matches its stated 2034–2040 window, and the-silence's probability was inverted (0.35→0.65). Seven signals or grading tests were rewritten so lines can actually be graded (fusion 'net electricity', 'continuously occupied', humanoid threshold, the Paris 20-year mean, deployment vs research for geoengineering). Added: labs-pace-the-frontier (2027), state-ai-laws-preempted (2027), helion-delivers-microsoft (2028), bci-permanent-approval (2029), china-crewed-moon (2030), fossil-co2-peak (2030). Indicators: open-weights-gap +0.3→+0.25, compute-ownership −0.2→−0.25, research-loop and who-decides 0→+0.1, compute-treaty −0.1→0, incidents +0.1→0. First observed anchors: population 8.2bn (2024, UN), warming 1.60/1.47°C (2024/2025, Copernicus), lifespan 83 (2023), 10 people off Earth, frontier-actors rebased to ~10. A source registry (SOURCES.md, data/sources.json) now drives the brief. Weak spots: Anthropic's R&D figure is self-reported; the Hugging Face incident details come from HF's technical timeline relayed by trade press; NASA briefed new Artemis dates today and the lunar line should be re-checked next week.

headline: One book, one strip; what counts is now a field; hinge is one number
body: Merged the illustrated-book redesign with the data figures: every page now shows a figure drawn from the forecast's own numbers (stripes, field of 100, curve with the UN reference line, clock, orbits) or a milestone ladder of what has to happen first (drugs, lunar base, fusion, Helion, BCI, China's Moon, Mars). Navigation is one strip plus an Overview of the whole century; page-turn links, the second nav and the index are gone. Data: every line now carries a timing (around / by / window / through) and 17 carry a resolution test stated in advance, moved out of prose into a field and sharpened where the old test was weaker than the headline (agents, R&D loop, humanoids, CO₂ peak, election, compute talks). The hinge is one number: 57% pluralism everywhere, scenario odds re-weighted (flourish 45 → 44, extinction 5 → 6). Fixed a stale 15% on mass-casualty-event and the Clock line's rationale (the Bulletin already weighs climate, bio and AI). Probability moves in history now carry from/to so resolved lines can be Brier-scored against the number they were written with. No probabilities changed in this revision.

headline: Four driver lines added: in-body gene editing, post-quantum migration, quantum chemistry, data-center power
body: The review found the forecast had nothing on gene editing, quantum, or electricity as the binding constraint on AI. Added, each with opened primary sources: in-vivo-editing-common-disease (2029–2031, 0.55: an in-body CRISPR/base/prime editor approved for a condition with over 100,000 US patients; lonvo-z for HAE is the platform proof, nex-z for ATTR-CM and VERVE-102 are the candidates), federal-pqc-deadline-met (2030, 0.20: EO 14412 sets 31 December 2030 for post-quantum key establishment on federal high-value systems; GAO's October 2026 audit found none of the 24 CFO Act agencies with the practices in place), quantum-chemistry-advantage (2030–2033, 0.40: a verified chemistry result on error-corrected hardware beating the best classical method; IBM's July 2026 70-logical-qubit result is a sampling benchmark, not chemistry), data-centres-tenth-us-power (2030, 0.50: LBNL puts data centers at 4.7% of US electricity in 2024 and 9.5–15.3% in 2030; ERCOT froze new large-load interconnections in August 2026). Each carries a resolution test and the condition that would make it a miss.

headline: Interactive field guide; evidence labels and versioned scoring
body: Added six interactive exhibit types. Corrected the hiring figure to the 19% relative employment gap; removed stale probability overrides and the unsupported 1,000-qubit threshold. Every line now has a versioned definition or an explicit unscored-scenario designation. Newly operationalized thresholds are editorial choices, not independently calibrated odds. Resolutions need evidence and a matching frozen definition; late outcomes no longer automatically count as successes. Five broad scenarios remain unscored. Timing labels, relationship types and source limitations are explicit. Probability values are unchanged. Six priority contextual claims were checked against primary sources; this is not a full re-verification of the citation registry.

headline: Review of the interactive-exhibit pass: kept the exhibits and versioned tests, removed the hedging
body: Kept: the six stage explainers, versioned resolution tests frozen in vintages, the compute-ownership wording fix, the native overview dialog with search, the deploy rollback copy. Reversed: scoring that could never use the forecast's founding odds (lines are now scored against the earliest vintage holding the same question, with any later rewording shown as a caveat); a 'subjective forecast' label under every percentage, boilerplate evidence notes on 36 lines and a boilerplate 'general challenge' in every drawer; placeholder signals on six far-future lines, replaced with real ones; the eight-forecast highlights tour (a second way to read); the resolution test folded away on desktop; the cornerstone title reworded to jargon; the site caveat rewritten into legalese. Helion keeps its dated milestone ladder instead of the generic fusion diagram. No probabilities changed.

headline: Twelve lines the forecast was missing: war, money, health, the planet, and the world outside the US
body: The forecast read as Silicon Valley's century. Added, each with a stated test, a miss condition and opened primary or institutional sources: autonomous weapons used at scale in a war between states (by 2028, 75%); a Taiwan Strait blockade or war cutting leading-edge chips for 90 days (2026–2032, 15%); the nuclear taboo holding through 2060 (68%, so 32% that a weapon is used); the AI trade halving (SOX 50% off its record, 2027–2030, 50%; it is already 26% down); AI showing in US productivity statistics (three years above 2.5%, 2032–2036, 50%); another pandemic with a million confirmed deaths (by 2050, 40%); a quarter of US adults on a GLP-1 (around 2032, 35%); the first ice-free Arctic September (2036–2050, 55%); a daily AI tutor for most teenagers in three OECD countries (around 2030, 50%); provenance rules for political ads (around 2028, 35%); India as the largest country on a frontier assistant (around 2028, 60%); Africa's working-age population passing China and India combined (2054–2062, 80%, the UN dates the crossing to 2058). Eleven existing lines gained a link to the new ones. The weave changed with them: climate and energy became a fourth force, every line is tagged with its force, chapter pages say where each thread stands, and every page says how old someone born in 2026 is when it happens. population-peak is now a cornerstone. A fact the forecast had not absorbed surfaced in the research and is recorded here for the next check-in: the United States and Israel have been at war with Iran since 28 February 2026 (CFR Global Conflict Tracker), with Khamenei killed, the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed for a period and merchant ships still being hit in October; the energy, risk and clock lines should be re-read against it.

headline: Evidence becomes explorable; grading matches the frozen question
body: Added UN age-group variants and NSIDC September observations, connected chapter threads and a return-visit revision digest. Aligned three headlines to their tests, removed the autonomous-weapons count loophole, separated unlike chart measures, corrected source attribution and restored evidence-backed scoring against the exact question. No probabilities moved.

headline: Review of the evidence-exhibit pass; a roadmap
body: Kept: the UN population and NSIDC Arctic exhibits with pinned source extracts, the probability-history strip in the drawer, the return-visit digest, thread buttons on chapter pages, CI in workflows. Changed: the per-chapter thread sentences are back (they had been replaced by a decorative diagram), the ruler reads 'a child born in 2026 is N' again, three titles return to plain language (titles are the claim; tests carry the precision), and scoring is now two numbers rather than a third reversal: a founding score against the earliest vintage holding the same claim, and a strict score against the identical frozen test with a sourced adjudication. The policy is written in CHECKIN.md. docs/ROADMAP.md sets out the next two quarters by track. No probabilities changed.
